Is the claim consistent with energy conservation?
questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Cyclic Heat Engines and Energy Flows under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Equation \([4]\) requires the output power to equal the difference between the heat-transfer rates: \[P_{\mathrm{out}}=\dot Q_H-\dot Q_C=80\,\mathrm{kW}-50\,\mathrm{kW}=30\,\mathrm{kW}.\] The claimed flows would account for \(50\,\mathrm{kW}+40\,\mathrm{kW}=90\,\mathrm{kW}\) leaving while only \(80\,\mathrm{kW}\) enters. Final result: the claim is inconsistent; a cyclic engine with those heat flows can deliver only \(30\,\mathrm{kW}\).

Final answer:
The claim is inconsistent; a cyclic engine with those heat flows can deliver only \(30\,\mathrm{kW}\).
